references.text: The same command to build an altar of stone without using iron tools, to preserve the natural state of the stones as holy to the Lord.
Joshua fulfills this command by building an altar of uncut stones on Mount Ebal, just as Moses had commanded.
Elijah builds an altar of stones for the Lord, in line with the tradition of using natural, unworked stones.
The basic instruction to build an altar of earth or stone for the Lord, which forms the background for the prohibition against iron tools.
The continuation of the instruction emphasizing that the altar must be built from whole, uncut stones.
